1.explanation: The root of the bug lives in the OrderedList React component (OrderedList.js). In the shipped Carbon code, this component always renders an <ol> with the class bx--list--ordered, which in the stylesheet applies counter-reset: item and populates numbers via ::before. The component’s signature in this snapshot no longer accepts or passes down a useNativeStyles prop (it was stripped out of the destructuring and classnames invocation), so consumers cannot opt out of Carbon’s custom counter. Restoring the useNativeStyles prop, applying the bx--list--native modifier class when it’s true, and updating the component’s tests and stories to include this variant will allow developers to remove the custom counter and fall back to native <ol> decimal numbering in Firefox.
1.bug_scenario: When using Carbon’s OrderedList component in Firefox, list numbering jumps to an arbitrary start (e.g. 7) because Carbon’s CSS applies a custom counter via counter-reset: item and ::before pseudo elements. Attempts to override that CSS via inline styles (counter-reset: unset/null) don’t work, so the only way to restore native decimal numbering is to remove the custom counter altogether. Users need a way to opt into the browser’s native ordered-list styles (decimal numbering) rather than Carbon’s custom counter scheme.

2.explanation: The OrderedList component is where the Carbon ordered‐list classnames are applied. Currently it doesn’t accept a prop to opt into native browser styles, so it always emits the `.bx--list--ordered` class which triggers the custom counter and pseudo‐element in the stylesheets. To fix the issue, OrderedList.js needs a new prop (e.g. `useNativeStyles`) that adds a modifier class (such as `.bx--list--native`) when true. The corresponding SCSS for `.bx--list--ordered` must be updated to skip `counter-reset: item` and the `::before` numbering when that modifier class is present. In addition, the test file (OrderedList-test.js) will need to be updated to assert that the new class is applied correctly.
2.bug_scenario: In Firefox the custom Carbon ordered‐list styles use a CSS counter (`counter-reset: item`) and a `::before` pseudo‐element to render list numbers, but this counter is misbehaving (starting at an arbitrary value) when overriding Carbon’s styles. Simply overriding `counter-reset` in user CSS doesn’t work; the only way to get a correct, native-style numbered list is to remove the counter rule entirely. The user needs a way to opt into native `decimal` list styling (no counter, no pseudo element).
